_note: Destructible field objects. NOT harvest nodes -- see src/sim/entities.ts on Prop.drops, and world.ts on why weapons must never touch a node. These are the other half of that rule: weapons DO break these, tools never do.
_spriteNote: Every sprite here is one the renderer already scattered as inert peripheral scenery. The list was split by whether the thing LOOKS LIKE IT HOLDS SOMETHING -- drum, barrel, bale, bin, cans, crate, barrow, trough, log and bone pile are breakable; the scarecrow, plough, grave marker, fence and barbed wire stay wallpaper. That split is the whole tutorial: a player never has to be told which scenery pays out, because containers do and fixtures do not.
_pierceNote: Breaking one costs the player NOTHING. A projectile that hits a breakable damages it and keeps its pierce, so a drum standing between the gun and the crowd is never a DPS tax. Consuming pierce here was the obvious implementation and would have made scenery a punishment -- the wave does not pause while you shoot furniture, so any bullet a crate ate would be damage the crowd did not take.
_aimNote: Breakables are a FALLBACK aim target, never a competing one. `findNearestEnemy` is asked first and only when it comes back empty does the aim fall to a breakable. Letting them into the normal target set would have weapons turn away from the wave to shoot a barrel, which is the same bug as the old weapons-damage-nodes one wearing a different hat.
_dropNote: The owner's brief: 'usually nothing, sometimes XP or food, rarely gear'. Held to literally -- `nothing` is the single heaviest row in every table. A breakable that always paid would be a node, and the game already has nodes.
_hpNote: Flat hp, no per-wave scaling. Nodes scale because the pickaxe ladder scales with them; nothing the player buys makes them break breakables faster, so scaling these would just make late scenery unbreakable.

magnet._note: The owner asked for 'a magnet object that drops occasionally and collects all items, power up to go with it'. Both halves: collecting it sweeps the field NOW (the same call a cleared wave makes), and then leaves the pickup radius hugely enlarged for a few seconds so everything that drops during the window walks itself in.

gear._note: A field-dropped item card. It is drawn from the SAME pool the shop and level-up offers use, and it respects maxStacks -- a gear drop that handed over a fourth copy of a three-stack item would be a dead pickup that looked like a reward.
